name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
summary: Amsterdam research university with 19 English-taught bachelor's, from AI, econometrics and maths to PPE, Law in Society and psychology.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma meets the entry rule. English: an English-taught or bilingual IB, or English A Lang & Lit SL 7/HL 6. Maths AA HL for econometrics, maths, CS, Business Analytics; none in social sciences, humanities, law.

apply.via: Studielink, then the VU dashboard on vu.nl

dates.label: VU Bachelor's Day on campus (6 and 7 November)
Enrolment: tuition fee paid (15 July for numerus fixus programmes)

programmes.name: Artificial Intelligence
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.about: AI designed to work with people (hybrid intelligence): machine learning and reasoning applied to healthcare robots, smarter triage, misinformation and sustainable energy, with attention to trust and responsibility.
programmes.overview: The focus is hybrid intelligence: AI that works with people, and is designed to be effective, trustworthy and socially responsible. Year one builds computational thinking and how AI interacts with people; year two applies this to real cases, such as programming a robot for a real environment or using AI for challenges in healthcare and law. Electives let you lean toward the social side of AI or toward technical depth in algorithms, data and computer science. In year three you take a minor, which can be abroad, and write a bachelor's thesis. Graduates work as software developers, data scientists, machine learning engineers or analysts, or continue to a master's in AI.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Business Analytics
programmes.about: Mathematics, data analysis, computer science and business combined to turn data into decisions, from stock levels to seat pricing; the programme has run at VU for more than 35 years.
programmes.overview: The programme is about half data analysis and mathematics, a third computer science and the rest business, and is taught by both the mathematics and computer science departments. Year one covers calculus, Python programming, linear algebra, probability, operations research and accounting, with practical projects. Year two adds statistics, stochastic modelling, R, C++ and SQL, business intelligence, finance and a big data project. In year three you take a minor, machine learning and combinatorial optimisation, and a group Bachelor Project: Business Case with an external company. Cases have involved IBM, Deloitte and Dutch Railways, and exchange places are available.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Communication and Information Studies
programmes.ib: Two English tracks: Language and Media, and Applied Linguistics; the Media and Journalism track is taught in Dutch.
programmes.about: How communication works and what language does in it, from persuasion on social media to the words that trigger associations. Two English tracks: Language and Media, and Applied Linguistics.
programmes.overview: You study how communication works and what role language plays in it, choosing a track from year one; the English-taught tracks are Language and Media and Applied Linguistics. Language and Media covers discourse analysis, global English, multilingual communication in the EU, visual design, language policy in organisations and how organisations use media with business and consumers. Applied Linguistics covers language structure, child language acquisition, language disorders, multilingualism and the role of large language models. Year three offers a minor or an internship, then social media analytics and a bachelor's thesis based on your own research. The small scale gives plenty of contact with lecturers.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Communication Science
programmes.about: A scientific approach to media and communication, from misinformation on social media to reputational damage, with a research project on a topic of your choice every semester.
programmes.overview: You study how people use media and communicate, drawing on psychology, sociology, media studies and marketing. Year one covers media use and organisational communication, with courses in journalism and interpersonal communication; year two turns to marketing and political communication, including the psychology of persuasion, health campaigns and social media analytics. Four project-based courses link study to professionals, and research methods and statistics run alongside. In year three you choose an internship, study abroad or a minor, and write a bachelor's thesis. Graduates work as communication advisers, PR officers, campaign designers, media analysts and journalists.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Computer systems from top to bottom, from algorithms and AI to chips, networks and cybersecurity, learning to build software that is secure, scalable and correct from active researchers.
programmes.overview: Year one gives a broad base: programming, logic, data structures and algorithms, web technology, computer organisation, networks, requirements engineering and a Systems Programming Project in which you design and build a computing system. Year two covers operating systems, databases, software design and functional programming, plus three electives such as AI or software engineering. In year three you take a semester-long minor, for example Bioinformatics or Business Analytics and Data Science, then automata, machine learning, ethics and a Bachelor's Project supervised by researchers. Graduates work as software developers, data scientists and IT consultants, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
programmes.about: How people live together and respond to change, from climate and migration to inequality and identity, studied from within through fieldwork and attention to culture, power and identity.
programmes.overview: You study how culture, power and identity shape each other in issues such as climate, migration and inequality. Year one covers anthropological theory, ethnographic and social research methods, the global history of inequality and statistics, with masterclasses on three professional tracks: researcher, practitioner and creative professional. In year two you choose a profile and study development, political and economic anthropology, nation and migration, and urban studies. Year three centres on ethnographic fieldwork for a Bachelor Project in the Netherlands or abroad, including Colombia, ending in an academic article, a policy report or a documentary, photo or podcast project.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Econometrics and Data Science
programmes.about: Econometric models combined with machine learning and time-series methods to forecast and decide, from a bank predicting inflation to a supermarket planning fresh stock.
programmes.overview: You learn to solve problems in economics and business with econometric models, machine learning, time series and statistics, for example predicting inflation or forecasting inventory. Year one covers calculus, linear algebra, programming, statistics, finance and macroeconomics, with an introduction to data science. Year two adds data structures, econometrics, databases and a small-group Data Science Project on real cases. In year three you take a minor or study abroad, take machine learning and robust statistics, and write a thesis on a topic you choose. Group work and company contacts run through the degree, and the study association organises company visits.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
programmes.about: Quantitative tools for economic and operational decisions, such as how financial shocks spread between banks or how hospitals can best use beds and doctors.
programmes.overview: You use quantitative techniques to investigate and solve problems in economics, business and finance, from banking systems to healthcare resources. Year one covers calculus, programming, linear algebra, probability, macroeconomics and finance, with an introduction to the three specialisation areas. Year two goes deeper into econometrics, operations research and mathematical economics, with numerical methods, case studies and group projects. In year three you take a minor or study abroad, choose a specialisation in econometrics, operations research or mathematical economics, and write a thesis on a subject of your interest. Minors range from closely related fields to political science.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Economics
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, Maths AI HL, or Maths AI SL at grade 5.
programmes.about: How consumers, firms and governments behave in economic systems, from single purchases to global decisions, with questions such as how to stop a bank collapsing.
programmes.overview: Year one covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, accounting, finance, marketing, programming for economists and quantitative research methods, and ends with an essay and the choice between General Economics and Business Economics. In year two, business economists specialise in accounting, finance or marketing, with courses in research methods, ethics, law and a research paper, in smaller groups. In year three you design the first semester yourself: a minor, for instance in psychology or sociology, study abroad or an internship. The second semester is for the thesis and your specialisation, and all courses are taught in English.

needs.note: Maths AI SL at grade 5 is also accepted.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: History and International Studies
programmes.about: The historical origins of today's global society, such as democracy, inequality and climate change, studied beyond Eurocentric perspectives and with attention to marginalised voices.
programmes.overview: You study Western and non-Western history from antiquity onward together with international relations. Year one covers academic skills, modern Europe, world history from 1000 to the present, and current debates in global history. In year two you choose a regional focus, such as Southeast Asia, Latin America, sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East or China, and take courses like Capitalism and Inequality, Oral History and History by Numbers, with research seminars. In the first semester of year three you can do an internship, study abroad or take a minor, then work on independent research for a bachelor thesis.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: International Business Administration
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, Maths AI HL, or Maths AI SL at grade 5.
programmes.about: Business in an international setting: marketing across cultures, corporate social responsibility and responsible finance, and working in diverse virtual teams.
programmes.overview: Year one covers business mathematics, organisation theory, global sustainability, accounting and global supply chain management, with a mentoring programme and academic skills. Year two adds business information systems, economics in a global era, finance, and qualitative and quantitative research methods, plus electives. Year three starts with a compulsory semester abroad at one of more than 150 partner universities, then electives, an ethics course and a bachelor's thesis. The IBA Lab has you work with real organisations on complex business challenges, and research participation courses build research skills.

needs.note: Maths AI SL at grade 5 is also accepted.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Law in Society
programmes.ib: Selective: a motivation-based application form, and possibly a Zoom interview.
programmes.about: A broad legal education (LLB) combined with social science research methods, applied to terrorism, corporate environmental damage, platform workers and asylum.
programmes.overview: Instead of the usual legal divisions, the programme is built around four themes: security, migration, sustainability and market globalisation, showing how several areas of law meet in one social problem. Year one covers security, with criminology, terrorism and philosophy of law, and then markets, including the platform economy, with statistics and psychology. Year two covers migration law and global migration governance and then sustainability, climate change, AI and law and ethics. Sociology, psychology and criminology run through the degree. Year three has a minor, a bachelor's thesis and recap courses in criminal, public and private law.

needs.note: Any IB maths; otherwise pass a maths entry test (VWO Maths C or OMPT-E).

programmes.selectionNote: Selective on motivation: an application form assessed monthly by the Admission Board, sometimes a Zoom interview. Apply early; final EU deadline 1 May.

programmes.name: Literature and Society: English
programmes.about: Literature and culture in English linked to social and political questions past and present, alongside other storytelling such as film, TV series and comics.
programmes.overview: You explore how literature, language and creativity shape society, reading canonical and contemporary English-language literature from the early modern period onward alongside film, television, comics, graphic novels and digital media. The programme combines literary study with linguistics, creative writing and the practice of the publishing industry, and looks at how technology, including AI, changes the way language and literature are produced. It links historical voices to current social, political and cultural questions. Graduates can aim at editorial and publishing work such as editing, copyediting and marketing.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Mathematics
programmes.about: A thorough foundation in pure and applied mathematics, from primes in cryptography to maths behind AI and animal skin patterns, with a data-driven or research-oriented path later on.
programmes.overview: Year one covers linear algebra, calculus, discrete mathematics, group theory, analysis, probability and Python programming, with mathematical modelling and typesetting skills. In year two you choose one of seven paths: Algebra and Geometry, Analysis and Dynamical Systems, Probability and Statistics, Biomedical Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, or Optimisation and Economics, with Fourier analysis, numerical methods and a Project Mathematics course. Year three includes a minor, or an education track toward teaching in secondary schools, and a Bachelor Project, which can be built on an internship with an outside organisation.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Media, Art, Design and Architecture
programmes.about: Images, objects and buildings studied together and in context, from Instagram as a museum to tiny houses, tracing their contested histories in a mediated, global world.
programmes.overview: A common first year covers visual and material culture, European cultural history, the history of media, art, design and architecture, image and object analysis and research methods. In year two you choose Media, Art, Design or Architecture, with track courses such as film and media history, modern art, graphic design and fashion theory, or urbanism and landscape architecture, plus shared courses on exhibitions and urban culture, and an excursion abroad. Year three has five months of free study, a minor, research internship or semester abroad, followed by a research seminar and a bachelor thesis.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Philosophy
programmes.ib: Apply for Philosophy in Studielink, then confirm the English-taught track in your VU dashboard.
programmes.about: Fundamental questions about knowledge, reality and justice asked about current themes, building a critical perspective on science, religion and society. Choose the English track after applying.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces logic and argumentation, epistemology, ethics, philosophy in global antiquity and contemporary European thought. Year two covers historical, practical and theoretical philosophy, from analytic philosophy and political philosophy to metaphysics and philosophy of mind, with two text seminars and electives. In year three you take a minor from another faculty and two electives, and write a thesis with training and tutoring support, choosing your own topic, problem and supervisor. English and Dutch tracks are offered, and a second study programme can be combined with philosophy.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE)
programmes.ib: Selective: 31 points excl. TOK and EE (2025-26 list; 2027 not yet published), motivation, maybe an interview. Maths AA SL/HL, AI HL or AI SL at 5.

separateFrom.name: Philosophy
separateFrom.reason: A different degree (BSc, not BA): selective, with 31 points, a motivation, perhaps an interview and a maths requirement Philosophy does not have.

programmes.about: A small, intensive programme combining philosophy, politics and economics to tackle questions of fairness, democracy, economic crises and environmental policy.
programmes.overview: Year one has core courses in ethics, microeconomics and political science, with mathematics, logic and statistics and PPE in Practice courses linking theory to real problems. In year two you choose two of three tracks, philosophy, politics or economics, such as political philosophy, global governance and international relations, or macroeconomics and policy, with electives like global justice, EU studies or behavioural economics. Year three lets you study abroad or do a five-month internship, and ends with a thesis. Graduates work as policymakers, consultants, reporters or academics in banks, governments, think tanks and universities.

needs.note: Maths AI SL at grade 5 is also accepted.

programmes.selectionNote: Selective: your GPA (Dutch 7.0 equivalent; at least 31 IB points excluding the core), motivation and fit, judged as one dossier; some are interviewed.

programmes.name: Political Science: Global Politics
programmes.about: Politics at the global level: international power relations and how they affect different societies, for careers taking part in or critically following politics.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces comparative politics, international relations, the politics of social problems, research methods, statistics and political thought, with visits to political institutions and Model United Nations exercises. Year two covers global governance, global political economy, the EU in the global order, and quantitative and qualitative research projects, plus Social Science for Society electives with sociology and communication science students. In year three the first semester is free for study abroad, an internship such as at an embassy or NGO, or a minor in social sciences, economics or law. The second semester is a Graduation Project Global Politics.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete your VU application.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus (600 places, English and Dutch tracks together): apply by 15 January; GPA plus an online test on 6 March 2027 (pass mark 5.5 of 10), then a lottery.
programmes.about: Why people think, feel and behave as they do, and how brain, personality, genes, environment and relationships shape it, applied to health, work, media and sport.
programmes.overview: The programme starts broad and then specialises. Year one covers biological, cognitive, social and developmental psychology, personality, psychopathology, research methods, statistics and communication skills. Year two adds neuropsychology, work and organisational psychology, genes and environment, interviewing skills and diagnostics, with pre-minors that preview year three. In year three you choose a learning line: Clinical, Psychopathology, Health and Prevention, Social and Organisational Psychology, or Genes, Cognition and Behaviour. You also take a minor and write an independent bachelor's thesis.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus, 600 places (English and Dutch tracks). Apply by 15 Jan 2027; GPA plus an online test on 6 March sort you into groups, then a lottery within groups 2 and 3.

notes: Binding study advice: you need at least 42 of 60 first-year credits (EC) to continue, 48 in International Business Administration and 54 in PPE.
Applicants with a diploma from outside the Netherlands pay a non-refundable €100 application fee, and VU's housing offer for internationals covers the first year only.
Mechanical Engineering and Creative Technology run mostly on VU's campus but you apply to the University of Twente; from 2027 Ancient Studies and Archaeology are applied for via UvA.
